# Rocketwind — Tailwind-style CSS, generated by Go

If your Go app lets people build pages or edit their theme, the CSS you need
doesn't exist when you build the app. It depends on what someone saves tomorrow.

Rocketwind is being built to compile that CSS inside your Go process. No Node
process, no build step for each edit, and no need to ship every possible utility
class to every visitor.

**Work in progress.** Core utilities, variants, stylesheet directives and the
Go plugin API work. The dynamic settings API, standard plugins, CLI and
compatibility profiles are still being built.
See [WORK.md](WORK.md) for the implementation gates.


Why?
----

Three things that are awkward with a conventional CSS build:

* **Generate CSS on the fly.** A template, page builder or plugin introduces
  `grid-cols-3` after your binary has shipped. Compile what it uses when you load
  the template, and cache the result.
* **Give each account its own CSS.** Different organizations choose different
  colors, fonts, spacing and components. Compile a stylesheet for each account
  from its configuration, without rebuilding your application.
* **Let people edit settings.** A theme editor stores a heading size and a brand
  color. A component can say `text-{heading.size} bg-{brand.color}`. Your code
  supplies the values and their types; Rocketwind turns them into CSS for a
  named class such as `.signup-button`.

The last case matters because Tailwind's names can be ambiguous. `text-*` can
mean a font size or a color. A setting's type should settle that question even
when its value is a CSS variable. Rocketwind must not guess from its name.

Ordinary helper classes work too: pass in `text-xl`, `hover:flex` and the other
classes your templates use, and get a stylesheet back. Configuration can come
from Go; you don't need a single entry-point CSS file.

```go
compiler := rocketwind.New(rocketwind.Config{
    Theme: map[string]string{"--color-brand": "#663399"},
})
css, err := compiler.Build([]string{"grid", "p-4", "text-xl", "bg-brand"})
```

Or start with a stylesheet containing `@theme`, `@utility`, `@apply` and
`@tailwind utilities`, using `rocketwind.Compile(css, config)`. Imports can use
`Config.LoadStylesheet`; Go configuration and plugins use `Config.LoadModule`.
The standard Tailwind theme and preflight stylesheet are built in.


Tailwind compatibility
----------------------

| Version | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Tailwind CSS **4.3.4** | Current target. All 2,144 compiler calls captured from nine upstream suites match exactly, plus 222 CSS parser calls and 66 arbitrary-value decoding calls. The full upstream suite is not yet ported, so complete compatibility is not yet verified. |
| Tailwind CSS **3.4.17** | Planned compatibility profile for existing applications. Not yet implemented or verified. |

The goal is to reproduce the core compiler and standard plugins in Go, including
their upstream tests. Running JavaScript configuration or arbitrary JavaScript
plugins is outside the scope. Those extensions need Go implementations.

Version compatibility includes defaults and generated CSS, not just accepting
the same class names. An older application must be able to keep its existing
styles while adopting Rocketwind. New templates should be able to use the
current version. Utilities already supplied by another stylesheet must not be
generated twice.

The library currently has **zero dependencies**. JavaScript tools are used only
to run upstream tests and capture reference results during development.
